January, February, March

The paragraph presents several legal issues regarding the enforceability of the non-disclosure agreement (NDA) and the validity of the termination. First, the absence of a witness to the signing raises questions about the formal execution of the contract. While many jurisdictions do not strictly require witnesses for NDAs, the lack thereof may impact the evidentiary weight of the signature or suggest procedural defects depending on specific state laws or company policies. Second, Alex’s claim of being unaware of the restrictions touches on the issue of mutual assent and informed consent. For an NDA to be enforceable, the employee generally must have had reasonable notice of its terms and an opportunity to review them. If Alex was not made aware of the document or its contents prior to signing, this could constitute a lack of meeting of the minds, potentially rendering the agreement unenforceable. Finally, the challenge to the termination itself hinges on whether the NDA is legally valid; if the court finds the NDA unenforceable due to the aforementioned issues, the termination for violating it may be deemed wrongful.
